current_experience: Has helped younger students read and organized one craft activity.

sessions.student_message: Which beginner activity would let me compare elementary teaching with library services?
sessions.expected_behavior: Offer an accessible way to compare teaching and library services. Explicitly connect the response to English 9 (grade 9), Child Development (grade 10) and Early Childhood Education (grade 11). Use stated marks only if useful.

follow_ups.student_message: I'd like to explore illustration too. What is a small sketchbook project I could try this week?
follow_ups.expected_behavior: Treat illustration as the current interest. Suggest one project, connect it to at least one applicable course per grade year when useful, and avoid framing it as the prior interest or changing the saved profile.

sessions.student_message: Today I'd like to switch to game design. What is a simple paper game I could make for younger readers?
sessions.expected_behavior: Recognize game design as the new interest after a reload. Suggest a small paper prototype and link it to the three course years without continuing the earlier illustration suggestion.

sessions.student_message: Help me make a two-session plan to practice explaining a math concept to a younger student.
sessions.expected_behavior: Suggest a manageable two-session teaching plan. Explicitly connect the response to Algebra I (grade 9), Child Development (grade 10) and Early Childhood Education (grade 11). Use stated marks only if useful.

sessions.student_message: I explained fractions using paper shapes. The student understood halves but not quarters. How should I adjust?

actions.text: Try the same method for quarters

sessions.expected_behavior: Build on the learner's understanding of halves and break quarters into a smaller step. Explicitly connect the response to Algebra I (grade 9), Child Development (grade 10) and Early Childhood Education (grade 11). Use stated marks only if useful. Carry forward a concrete relevant detail from the earlier elementary teaching discussion when it helps, and keep the intervening illustration topic out of the answer.

sessions.student_message: How could I try taking a set of three portraits of objects using only window light?
sessions.expected_behavior: Address photography as the active interest and suggest a manageable starting project.

sessions.student_message: They can fold the square twice now, but still call every piece a half. What could I ask them to check?
sessions.expected_behavior: Infer the paper-folding fractions lesson. Prompt the learner to count the equal pieces that make the whole.
